SongComments.SongComment: This small tutorial shows the concept of Lines Per Beat (LPB).

The LPB value indicates how many lines make up a beat, allowing for higher or lower resolution within a beat. You can change the LPB value during the song using the command ZLxx, where xx is the number (in hexadecimal) of lines which will compose a beat starting from the line where the command is put.

Look at how the line colouring changes to highlight how the beat length changes. Also, notice how the frequency of hihat hits does not change along the pattern: there always is a hihat on each line, but the measure it represents depends on the LPB value: at first, with ZL01, each line is a beat, so the hihat will be played with a measure of 1/1; then, with ZL02, each line will have a measure of 1/2; at LPB 3 (ZL03), each line will be a measure of 1/3 and so on.
